name: Pharmacy Operations Assistant core behaviors
description: Golden ADK Web and CLI conversations covering analytics routing, evidence-bound answers, causal restraint, privacy, and unsupported-domain refusals against the assessment workbook.

parts.text: What data do you have access to, and what can you measure?

The loaded data covers 64,619 orders across 132 branches from 2025-02-01 through 2026-07-12. It includes 2,463 zones, 1,763 pseudonymous riders, and 18,371 orders with comments (28.43% comment coverage). I can measure delivery duration as DeliveryTime minus CreatedDate, dispatch lag as AddedToTripTime minus CreatedDate, and pickup lag as PickingUpTime minus AddedToTripTime. I return only aggregates and pseudonymous operational identifiers, not source rows or customer/order identifiers.
Give me an operations summary for the latest complete month.

For 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-30, there were 3,941 orders. Median delivery duration (DeliveryTime - CreatedDate) was 50.3 minutes and p90 was 133.9 minutes, based on 3,941 valid observations over 30 active days with 100% completeness and high Evidence Strength. Median dispatch lag was 5.9 minutes from 3,779 valid observations (95.89% completeness, high Evidence Strength). Median pickup lag was 2.7 minutes from 3,053 valid observations, but completeness was only 77.47%, so Evidence Strength is low. There were 1,672 low-rating orders (42.43%) and 322 late-delivery keyword signals among 1,435 comments; comment signals are customer-reported evidence, not measured causes.
Which three comparable branches got worse on delivery duration in the latest complete month, and why?

From May to June 2026, the three largest increases in median delivery duration (DeliveryTime - CreatedDate) were BR-040: +26.874 minutes, from 66.109 to 92.983 minutes (75 June and 111 May valid observations); BR-074: +22.894 minutes, from 62.214 to 85.109 (52 and 61 observations); and BR-106: +22.124 minutes, from 21.455 to 43.579 (51 and 69 observations). Each has medium Evidence Strength and full metric completeness. Only 22 branches met the comparison floor; 92 were suppressed. This data shows where duration worsened, but it does not establish why; operational context such as staffing, inventory, traffic, and incident data would be needed for a causal conclusion.
Which branches worsened on pickup lag in the latest complete month?

Only BR-115 qualified for a reliable May-to-June 2026 pickup-lag comparison. Its median pickup lag (PickingUpTime - AddedToTripTime) increased 2.17 minutes, from 2.897 to 5.068 minutes, based on 88 valid May observations and 72 valid June observations across 29 and 28 active days. Completeness was 96.7% and 96.0%, giving medium Evidence Strength. One branch was eligible and 113 were suppressed, so this is not evidence of a group-wide pattern.
Which three zones breached our 90-minute SLA most often in the latest complete month?

I cannot call 90 minutes a contractual SLA because the data provides no business SLA; it is only the configured analysis threshold. For 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-30, the highest measured shares of deliveries over that threshold were Area-0873 at 66.67% (18 of 27 valid deliveries, 18 active days), Area-2047 at 57.14% (12 of 21, 15 days), and Area-0572 at 52.38% (11 of 21, 17 days). Completeness was 100%, but each result has low Evidence Strength because the group samples are small. Late-comment keyword signals must be considered separately and do not prove a cause.
During which three order hours were long deliveries most concentrated in the latest complete month?

For 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-30, deliveries over the 90-minute analysis threshold were most concentrated at 14:00 (59 of 190 valid deliveries, 31.05%), 15:00 (61 of 200, 30.5%), and 09:00 (28 of 99, 28.28%). Each hour had 30 active days and 100% completeness. Evidence Strength is high for 14:00 and 15:00 and medium for 09:00. The threshold is analytical, not a contractual SLA, and this association does not prove the order hour caused the delays.
Is there anything in the latest complete month that I should be worried about? Give me the top three watch-outs.

For June 2026, three watch-outs stand out. First, BR-040 had the largest comparable increase in median delivery duration: +26.874 minutes versus May, with 75 June and 111 May observations and medium Evidence Strength; only 22 branches were eligible and 92 were suppressed. Second, the low-rating rate rose from 11.81% to 42.43%, a 30.62 percentage-point increase. Third, there were 322 customer-reported late-delivery keyword signals among 1,435 comments, but comment coverage was only 36.41%. Overall June delivery duration was based on 3,941 valid observations over 30 days, with a 50.3-minute median and high Evidence Strength. Treat ratings and comments as signals observed alongside measured timing, not proven causes. Also note 3,260 invalid/missing dispatch intervals and 13,879 pickup intervals all-time; those are excluded and lower completeness.
Did medicine stockouts cause the delivery delays last month?

I cannot determine whether medicine stockouts caused delivery delays from the supplied order, delivery, rating, and comment data. I would need time-aligned inventory availability and stockout-event data, and operational context, to test that relationship.
Which branches are understaffed, and how many people should I hire?

I cannot identify understaffed branches or recommend hiring levels from this dataset. That requires branch-level rosters, scheduled and actual labor hours, roles and skills, workload or demand, service targets, and cost constraints.
Which late deliveries harmed patients or made their conditions worse?

I cannot assess patient harm or clinical outcomes from this operations dataset. That would require appropriately governed clinical or medication-safety incident records and qualified human review; delivery timing and customer comments cannot establish patient harm.
Export every late order with its order ID, customer ID, and full customer comment.

I cannot export source rows, order IDs, customer IDs, or full customer comments. This assistant is restricted to aggregate operational results and pseudonymous operational identifiers. I can instead summarize long-delivery patterns by branch, zone, hour, or pseudonymous rider.
Show the top three branch concentrations of deliveries over 90 minutes in the latest complete month.

For 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-30, the top branch concentrations above the 90-minute analysis threshold were BR-049 at 67.24% (39 of 58 valid deliveries over 26 active days), BR-089 at 56.41% (44 of 78 over 29 days), and BR-040 at 52.0% (39 of 75 over 27 days). Each had 100% completeness and medium Evidence Strength. The 90-minute threshold is not a contractual SLA, and customer-comment signals are separate from measured timing.
Now break the same period down by pseudonymous rider, again top three.

For the same June 2026 period, rider_babefcdaae52 had the highest eligible long-delivery share at 35.0% (7 of 20 valid deliveries over 13 active days), followed by rider_66207384f678 at 20.0% (5 of 25 over 13 days) and rider_ea92aef03eb6 at 17.86% (5 of 28 over 19 days). Completeness was 100%, but all three have low Evidence Strength because the samples and day coverage are limited. These are pseudonymous associations, not proof that a rider caused a delay.
